messages.author: 5b0c9158bfa781ba
messages.subject: Tabsets and linked update
parts:
Hello,
I have tabset described below. When I press update, how can i simultaneously update both tabpanels?
Currently i have to press update on each one.

Thank you
Saptarshi

tabsetPanel(
              tabPanel("Overview",
                       h4("Summary"),
                       tableOutput("summary"),

                       h4("Quantile Plot"),
                       plotOutput("qplot"),
                       
                        h4("Execution Time"),
                        verbatimTextOutput("exectime")),
              tabPanel("Evolution",
                       h4("Time Series of Measure vs. Build ID selected"),
                       plotOutput("tplot"))

messages.subject: Re: Tabsets and linked update
parts:
submitButton is broken and terrible; among other things it does not play well with tabsets. One workaround is to use actionButton and isolate instead.

actionButton is part of shiny-incubator; you need to install it using:

install.packages("devtools")
devtools::install_github("shiny-incubator", "rstudio")

You can find out more about actionButton using its help topic. Here's a link that shows how you use the two features together.
https://groups.google.com/d/msg/shiny-discuss/l8ZcauoOtuw/0pYyU5slVgsJ

messages.author: 7befd1c701df2fda
messages.subject: Re: Tabsets and linked update
parts: I think there is still some problems with using tabset with actionbutton. For example, if you are currently one a tab that doesn't do computationally-intensive task, you will see the update right away. So far so good. But if there is a computationally-intensive task on the tab (in my case, it's graph), the content in that tab remains the same, even though it's doing some intensive computation and will return something to the user after a while. However, from the user's perspective, she won't know if the app is working hard to render the result. So this is not user-friendly. I would suggest give some kind of feedbacks to the user when the user switches to the computationally-intensive tab (like shading it), so that the user knows she should wait for the result.
